```json
{
  "subtype": "faceted_decomposition",
  "concept": "patient_needs",
  "per_column": [
    {
      "name": "clinical_problem_type",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "The nature of the clinical problem (acute, chronic, preventive, etc.) is a constitutive aspect of what a patient needs -- it characterizes the underlying need itself, not an external correlate."
    },
    {
      "name": "acuity_and_threat",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "The urgency/severity dimension of a patient's need is a genuine aspect of the need (how pressing the need is). It is a part-of decomposition, though it overlaps somewhat with the existing 'urgency' column and with clinical_problem_type's acute/chronic split."
    },
    {
      "name": "intervention_required",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "What intervention the patient requires (pharmaceutical, procedural, counseling) directly expresses the substance of the need -- what must be done for the patient. A legitimate facet."
    },
    {
      "name": "anatomic_system_focus",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "Which body system/domain the need concerns is an aspect of the need (its clinical locus). Constitutive, though values mixing anatomic systems with 'mental_health' and 'pediatric_developmental' blur the facet's basis."
    },
    {
      "name": "care_coordination_requirement",
      "is_constitutive_facet": true,
      "role": "facet",
      "rationale": "The coordination/follow-up a patient's care requires is a real aspect of the need -- the ongoing/logistical dimension. A distinct part-of facet."
    }
  ],
  "facet_columns": [
    "clinical_problem_type",
    "acuity_and_threat",
    "intervention_required",
    "anatomic_system_focus",
    "care_coordination_requirement"
  ],
  "non_facet_columns": [],
  "mutual_exclusivity": 0.7,
  "exhaustiveness": 0.8,
  "rationale": "All five columns are genuine part-of facets of 'patient_needs' (problem nature, acuity, required intervention, anatomic locus, and coordination requirement), so the meronymy test is satisfied across the board. Mutual exclusivity is good but not perfect: acuity_and_threat partly overlaps with the acute/chronic distinction embedded in clinical_problem_type, and anatomic_system_focus imports a 'mental_health' value that also appears in clinical_problem_type, creating cross-facet redundancy. Exhaustiveness is strong -- the set spans the problem, its severity, its treatment, its bodily domain, and its downstream coordination -- though patient-experienced/psychosocial or informational needs (e.g., patient understanding, social/support needs) are underrepresented, leaving some constitutive aspects only partially covered."
}
```
